title: The Error Hunt
description: Count today's ERROR lines in app.log and timestamp the last one for the incident ticket.
scenario: Users report intermittent failures on the staging API. Before escalating, the incident template requires two hard numbers from /var/log/app/app.log: how many ERROR lines occurred today, and the exact timestamp of the LAST error. Produce /home/intern/error-report.txt with `error-count=<n>` and `last-error=<YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS>`.
symptoms: app.log mixes INFO, WARN and ERROR lines
The incident template demands an error count and the last error's timestamp
No monitoring dashboard covers this app yet
mission: Create /home/intern/error-report.txt containing `error-count=7` and `last-error=2026-06-17 09:42:11`, both derived from the real log.

hints.title: Count with grep -c
hints.content: `grep -c ERROR file` prints only the number of matching lines — exactly the incident template's error-count.

hints.title: Log lines are chronological
hints.content: The LAST error is the last matching line: pipe the matches through `tail -1`.

hints.title: Extract the timestamp
hints.content: Each line starts 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS LEVEL ...', so `awk '{print $1, $2}'` on that one line gives '2026-06-17 09:42:11'.
